title: Angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor induced cough compared with placebo, and other antihypertensives: A systematic review, and network meta-analysis
authors: Hu Y, Liang L, Liu S, Kung JY, Banh HL
population: 135 randomised trials of eleven ACE inhibitors against placebo, angiotensin receptor blockers or calcium channel blockers
funder: not stated: the publication carries no funding statement. The authors declare no conflicts of interest.
authorConflicts: The authors declare no conflicts of interest.
result: Relative risk of cough with ACE inhibitors 2.21 (95% CI 2.05 to 2.39) against placebo, 3.2 (2.91 to 3.51) against angiotensin receptor blockers and 5.30 (4.32 to 6.50) against calcium channel blockers; angiotensin receptor blockers carried 2.03 (1.56 to 2.66) times the risk of calcium channel blockers. Ramipril against placebo 5.79 (2.61 to 12.88), lisinopril 4.39 (1.15 to 16.81), enalapril 2.9 (1.63 to 5.17); differences between individual ACE inhibitors were not significant. The authors cite reported cough incidence of 3.9% to 35%.
